newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian problem loans increase in November - ABI.
newsitem.headline: Italian problem loans increase in November - ABI.

text.p: Non-performing loans as a proportion of all Italian bank loans rose to 11.14 percent in November from 10.89 percent in October, a monthly report by the Italian banking association (ABI) said on Wednesday.
Calculated net of the estimated loss on their nominal value, non-performing loans amount to 6.70 percent of all loans in November, compared with 6.54 percent in October.
Non-performing loans on banks' books amounted to 118.368 trillion lire in November, a rise of 15.2 percent over the previous 12 months.
Net of the estimated loss on face value they rose three percent year-on-year in November to 71.122 trillion lire.
Banks were extending fewer loans to clients, reflecting the poor economic climate.

Lira loans in November rose 4.45 percent year-on-year to 778.5 trillion lire after a 5.88 percent increase in October while foreign currency loans fell 12.12 percent year-on-year to 76.5 trillion lire after a 14.53 percent decline in October. --Milan newsroom +392-66102321
